caseno: Writ Petition No. 2633 of 1998 with Writ Petition No. 3932 of 2001.

Rafiqul Huq with Md Zafarullah Chowdhury and Ahsanul Karim, Advocates -For the Petitioner. 
Abdur Rezaque Khan with Nesar Ahmed, Advocates -For Respondent No. 3. 
Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate-For Respondent No. 5.
parties:
Major Monjur Quader (Retd) ----- Petitioner 
Vs. 
Bangladesh Bank and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 16. It appears that the petitioner obtained a loan of Taka seventy lac from Sonali Bank for the purpose of construction of certain flats. Sanction letter of loan shows that the loan was issued on certain terms and conditions and, as such, when the petitioner failed to repay the installments in time, Sonali Bank in the normal course of business issued notice upon the borrower to repay the same. It has been submitted on behalf of the petitioner that he wanted to adjust the loan liability by selling out some of the flats but no permission was accorded by the bank. On the other hand, on behalf of the bank, it has been contended that they wanted certain clarification on the matter and had sent letters to the petitioner from time to time as reflected from Annexure 3 series in Writ Petition No. 3932 of 2001 but no reply was received by the bank authority and therefore, it could not accord the necessary permission. The petitioner's contention is that he did not receive the letters from the Bank as alleged and that the same not having been sent by registered post cannot create any presumption of being received by the petitioner. Whether, in fact, these letters were received by the petitioner or not is a question of fact which cannot be decided in this Writ Petition. Suffice it to say that there is no good reason why these letters should not be considered to have been sent by the bank; their alleged carbon copies have been shown to the Court (Annexure 3 series in Writ Petition No. 3932 of 2001). Mere denial by the petitioner of receiving the letters will not absolve him of his duty to furnish the particulars required by the bank. He had applied for permission to sell the flats and adjust the loan liability. We see no reason why the bank will withhold permission if the borrower cooperates. A creditor bank is always eager for its loan to be repaid by the borrower. In the circumstances, we feel that the petitioner's non repayment of loan to the bank due to the fault of the Bank by withholding permission to sell the flats has not been proved by the petitioner.
